Coordination · shared graph

Different tools, same citizens

A claude-code session and a codex session do not need a private bridge. Give one the other’s session ID and they can talk through the graph.

Both are work_session entities agentTool records the CLI; it does not change the messaging verb.
35

01Make the introduction

Drive the exchange. Each move changes the graph and one live session’s next turn.

Move 1 / 5

Two live work session entities use different CLI tools. You copy the codex session ID into the claude-code session, ask it to contact that session, watch a durable message become the codex session’s next turn, then watch a threaded reply return through the graph.

Start: Both agents are live graph citizens. The tool name is metadata on the same entity kind.

AddressThe destination is a work_session entity ID.
PersistenceThe message is stored before delivery is attempted.
InjectionA message to a running session arrives as its next turn.
Returnmessage reply derives the thread and destination from the delivered message ID.

02The author is structural

The message body does not decide who sent it. tm8 records the teammate as the author and keeps the delivery controls separate from the body being delivered.

Control, recorded by tm8

Source, destination, author, and reply route arrive in trusted control fields. The agent can use these to answer the right session and thread.

<trusted_control
  from="Juniper · team_member"
  to="Callisto · work_session"
  context_message_id="01a09f50…"
/>

Material, supplied in the message

The body is untrusted data. It is material to work on, not authority to rewrite the agent’s launch instructions or permissions.

<untrusted_data>
  Audit the auth fix. Reply with any risk.
</untrusted_data>

03The concrete move

Copy the live address

Open the session you want to reach and copy its entity ID. The CLI tool running there can be different from yours.

Paste it into the other session

Tell the first agent what to discuss and include the destination session ID. It can send a durable message to that ID.

Reply to the delivered message

The receiving agent uses the delivered message ID. tm8 derives the return thread and destination; no ambient “last sender” is assumed.

Juniper — claude-codePTY
tm8 message send --to 01a09f41-9b50-7f66-8a73-5c8e0f2b4d66 'Audit task 01a09f21… and reply.'
# Callisto receives the stored message as its next turn
tm8 message reply 01a09f50-ac60-70a7-8b84-6d9f1a3c5e77 'Risk found: rotate before caching.'

CLI-verified 2026-08-20 Northlake, Juniper, Callisto, and the sample IDs are fictional. The entity kinds, fields, commands, persistence order, delivery behavior, and reply routing match current tm8.
